uncited: It sets itself apart from [Ray Marching Jittering](5399-ray-marching-jittering.md) by applying perturbation to the UV coordinates rather than the step size, and from [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by focusing on geometric sampling stability rather than color interpolation.
*   Input: Current UV coordinates (`uv`), ray distance (`t`), dithering strength factor (`c_fDither`), and a pseudo-random number generator function (`rand`).
*   **Time Complexity:** O(1) per pixel per step, as it involves simple arithmetic and a random function call.
*   **Memory Complexity:** O(1), no additional data structures required.
Not suitable for all types of artifacts (e.g., step-size related aliasing is better handled by [Ray Marching Jittering](5399-ray-marching-jittering.md)).
*   **When to Use:** When banding artifacts are visible due to fixed step sizes or quantization in UV space.
*   **When Not to Use:** When high precision is required without any perturbation, or when step-size aliasing is the primary issue.
It is a technique used to improve the visual quality of ray-marched scenes by mitigating banding.
